article_framing_rejections.headline: Debbie Wasserman Schultz defeats Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick in redrawn Florida congressional district

lead_independence.headline: Debbie Wasserman Schultz defeats Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick in redrawn Florida congressional district
lead_independence.lead: Debbie Wasserman Schultz tearfully thanked voters for having confidence in her Tuesday night after defeating four Black primary opponents in a plurality Black district. The redrawn Florida 20th is concentrated in the most diverse parts of South Florida's Broward County and is the most Democratic House district in Florida, meaning she will be a prohibitive favorite in November. Wasserman Schultz, who is white and has served in Congress since 2005, was the only white candidate in the district. Her four Black primary opponents, including Cherfilis-McCormick, had argued that the district requires a Black representative, but voters went with a candidate who touted long experience.
